properties.name: Kathreiner Haus
properties.description:
The Kathreiner Haus demonstration, part of the EU Reincarnate project, shows how digital innovation can drive the transition to a circular economy in construction. In essence, the project introduces a parametric automation tool designed to seamlessly integrate reclaimed building components into Building Information Modeling (BIM) workflows. By leveraging Dynamo and Revit, the tool bridges the gap between digital marketplaces for second-hand materials and BIM models, enabling architects and engineers to efficiently match and reuse components while maintaining design flexibility.
The primary objective is to transform construction practices by reducing waste and carbon emissions through the systematic reuse of materials.

properties.name: High Rise Building
properties.description: This report presents an autonomous robotic system developed for on-site construction waste assessment and separation within the REINCARNATE project framework. The demonstration focuses on the Longhu Binjiang Tianjie construction site in Wuhan, China, where the system is deployed to support automated identification and handling of construction and demolition waste (CDW). Traditional waste sorting methods in construction environments often rely on manual labour, which can be inefficient and potentially hazardous.

properties.name: Office building of partner 3L (HQ)
properties.description:
The office building of project partner 3L was built in 1998 as a demonstration project
for the Federal State of North Thine Westfalia to show the feasibility to build buildings
using innovative assembly techniques avoiding wet construction methods. 
storey building with a floor area of 1100 m2 is composed of highly flexible steel frame
and lightweight construction components that are designed for modular dismantling
and reuse.

properties.name: Tiny House
properties.description:
We expect that people interested in tiny house, will also be more willing to adopt reused materials and building
products. Therefore, in this demonstration we will demonstrate the possibility to entirely built tiny houses from
reused materials and products. To this end, around all materials and products of all REINCARNATE demonstration
projects, project partner 3L will develop a parametric BIM-based design tool for tiny houses making use of existing
reused products and recycle materials at a specific time will be set-up. Additionally, possibilities for robotic
automation for assembling tiny houses will be explored using TUB robot cell. At project�s end, a tiny house
completely built from reused components and recycled materials will be built and show cased in Berlin.

properties.name: Circular housing asset management (HQ Paris Habitat)
properties.description:
Paris Habitat demonstration site � a 1950s social housing complex in Paris (15th arrondissement) comprised of three 12-story towers and one low-rise building (281 units). The renovation scenario needed to respect the dense urban context and various constraints.The French public housing organization Paris Habitat is an (inter)national frontrunner in using building adaptation
as an opportunity for generating new social housing, as well as incorporating re-use of building products in housing
refurbishment. Because of its size, Paris Habitat can
generate flows of building products and material within its own portfolio and, as part of the InterregNWE project
CHARM, it is developing an internal material exchange platform for facilitating exchange and re-use of building
components. In the project we will demonstrate how the innovative technologies from REINCARNATE can be used
to highly increase the efficiency and quality of data collection for the internal exchange platform and thereby
contributing to lowering organizational costs to the benefit of affordable housing.

properties.name: Supply chain cooperation demolition contractor and developer (Lagemaat )
properties.description:
In the construction sector, there is still little collaboration between architects and dismantling companies, while it
is precisely this collaboration that is crucial for circular construction and continued effective reuse of buildings and
components. Architects need insight into materials and products that are released through dismantling, so that
they can incorporate them in time in designs for new buildings. Dismantling companies need insight into the need
for released materials and products, so that they can adjust their dismantling and (temporary) storage accordingly.
The REINCARNATE innovations have the potential to facilitate this direct collaboration between demolition
companies and architects. This potential will be demonstrated in cooperation with architect/developer Cepezed
projects and demolition contractor Lagemaat B.V.

properties.name: TUB Building
properties.description:
This report presents an ML-based, non-destructive approach for the detection and assessment of cracks in masonry structures using image data. The work focuses on the application of machine learning and deep learning techniques to automatically identify and segment crack patterns, enabling a data-driven evaluation of structural condition.
A custom dataset of masonry surface images was collected and annotated to support supervised learning. The methodology combines traditional machine learning models with deep learning architectures to analyse visual features and spatial patterns associated with cracks. This enables both classification of crack presence and pixel-level segmentation of crack geometry.

properties.name: Three dedicated CDW management projects -Technical Heights building - Teknikh�jden
properties.description: The Technical Heights demonstration at Teknikh�jden in Stockholm is the most innovation-rich case in the REINCARNATE portfolio. The site � a 1960s educational building complex owned by Akademiska Hus, scheduled for demolition � served as a platform for validating five REINCARNATE innovations simultaneously through three interconnected sub-demonstrations: (i) Inventory of the Material Bank, (ii) Flat Glass to Flat Glass, and (iii) BIM-Supported Dismantling Planning (Plan B). The demonstration was coordinated across multiple partners and represented a genuine multi-actor, multi-method circular construction exercise under real project conditions.

properties.name: Timber house
properties.description: This report presents the application of non-destructive testing (NDT) methods for the condition assessment and serviceability evaluation of timber roof structures. The work focuses on identifying degradation mechanisms, particularly moisture-related damage, and assessing their impact on structural performance through in-situ measurements. Two real-world case studies, located in Werdau and Berlin-Pankow, are analysed using a combination of manual inspection techniques and continuous sensor-based monitoring to capture environmental conditions and material behaviour over time.

properties.name: Infrastructure Replication, Waste Water Treatment Plant
properties.description:
This demonstration project will try to replicate REINCARNATE innovations on a water
treatment plant project of partner VIAS. Water treatment plants are ideal examples of
complex urban projects to allow for demonstrating the wider applicability of REINCARNATE
solutions beyond buildings as they allow for the exploration of different, often
contaminated materials, but also include many construction products (pumps, valves, etc.)
that might lend themselves for reuse.

properties.name: Circularity metrics & data structures

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: Does not define construction-specific component identifiers, provenance chains, or handover protocols for components crossing organisational boundaries. REINCARNATE CP-IM uses JSON+REST; no normative counterpart exists.
properties.name: Material traceability & reuse workflows

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: No current ISO or CEN standard defines machine-readable traceability data for CDW fractions (concrete, brick, timber, glass) compatible with digital delivery tickets and CP-IM JSON. EN 50625 / ISO 15270 cover material codes only � full traceability chain is unstandardised.
properties.name: Material traceability & reuse workflows

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: IDM provides methodology for linking business processes to information delivery in BIM. No reuse-specific delivery specification exists. D5.3's gate-based process model is effectively a proto-IDM for reuse that should be developed into a normative specification.
properties.name: Material traceability & reuse workflows

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: No standard addresses ownership, liability, warranty, or guarantee framework for secondary/reclaimed construction materials crossing organisational boundaries.
properties.name: Material traceability & reuse workflows

properties.type_of_gap: No relevant content yet (AWI stage) � new standard
properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: ISO/AWI 59014 is an Active Work Item that will directly address secondary materials traceability � the core of REINCARNATE GAP 3.2 and GAP 3.4. At AWI stage, no content yet available. Critical opportunity: REINCARNATE evidence (CDW flows, CP-IM provenance fields, demo site data) can directly inform this standard. No construction-specific scope confirmed yet � there is a risk this becomes generic/non-construction-focused without sector input.
properties.name: Material traceability & reuse workflows

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: IFC is the backbone for BIM exchange across REINCARNATE. Revision extends infrastructure coverage but lacks standardised property sets for reuse classification, disassembly sequences, and circular potential. Extensions are project-specific and not normalised.
properties.name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability

properties.type_of_gap: Standard scope insufficient � reuse workflow absent
properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: ISO 19650 is the reference standard for CDE and information management. No part addresses reuse-specific workflows, component lifecycle tracking across ownership changes, or circular handover protocols. Certification cost is a cited barrier.
properties.name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability

properties.type_of_gap: Published TR � scope confirmed; reuse-specific API profiles still absent
properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: Will detail CDE as collaborative BIM workflow, including linking to Asset Management Systems and Open API for CDE (TC442 WG2). Does not address reuse-specific data storage or secondary material API profiles. CP-IM architecture extends beyond this TR.
properties.name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: Provides recommendations for BIM object library format and content. Does not define representation of reclaimed or upgraded components, or reuse-relevant properties (condition, origin, residual life). 3L's URRBC ontology is a reuse library extension with no normative standard to align to.
properties.name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: No current standard defines open API profiles or JSON data-exchange formats for circular component information management platforms (CP-IM equivalents). D5.3 Section 7.4 proposes submitting JSON templates and OpenAPI bundles to buildingSMART and CEN/TC 442.
properties.name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: Confirmed scope: manufacturer-to-designer data exchange for MEP building services equipment only. Not applicable to structural/envelope components (concrete, timber, brick, glass). Relevant only as a structural reference for how product catalogues could be extended.
properties.name: BIM fragmentation & interoperability

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: Provides guidance for organisations transitioning from linear to circular business models. Contains no operational templates for circular procurement criteria, reuse component tendering, or supply-chain validation.
properties.name: Circularity in procurement & value chains

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: EPD standard does not address EPDs for secondary or reclaimed materials, nor specify how recycled content and circular value flows are disclosed. BAM's SLAMD CO?-savings results have no standard EPD format.
properties.name: Circularity in procurement & value chains

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: Links EPD data to BIM workflows. Applicable only to virgin products with existing EPDs. No template or mechanism for reclaimed component sustainability declarations within BIM. REINCARNATE CO?-savings data lacks a standard BIM property set.
properties.name: Circularity in procurement & value chains

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: Establishes sustainability indicators for civil engineering works. Does not address circularity-specific indicators or reuse performance. Relevant to VIAS demo site.
properties.name: Circularity in procurement & value chains

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: Reviews characteristics of CE value networks. Not normative. Relevant as background for REINCARNATE's D5.2 value chain analysis. REINCARNATE data could enrich this TR.
properties.name: Circularity in procurement & value chains

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: No standard defines a re-certification or re-approval schema for construction products and components after removal from a building. In Germany (and likely Europe-wide), product approval (Zulassung) lapses at installation AND at removal. No standardised process for Second Life assessment of building components exists.
properties.name: Product re-certification & re-approval

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: No standard addresses ownership transfer, liability, warranty, or guarantee frameworks for secondary/reclaimed construction materials or components crossing organisational boundaries. Directly impedes market-scale reuse: actors cannot define contractual responsibilities without a normative reference. CP-IM records ownership and component history but has no normative liability framework to reference.
properties.name: Ownership & liability of secondary materials

properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: �NORM B 3151 (ASI) specifies selective deconstruction, mono-material separation, and hazardous substance identification � directly relevant to REINCARNATE's pre-demolition inventory and CDW traceability goals. DIN 18007:2022 provides German equivalent. Neither is a European standard; no CEN counterpart exists. Gap: no EN-level standard for selective deconstruction method with reuse-optimised separation requirements. REINCARNATE results (robotic deconstruction, HUST material codes, demo-site protocols) could support NWIP for EN-level standard.
properties.name: National & sectoral: deconstruction and CDW

properties.type_of_gap: Standard scope insufficient for high-quality reuse pathway
properties.missing_elements_and_limitations: EN 206 and EN 12620 include recycled aggregate provisions but with density limits and quality caveats. Expert 4 (VIAS) notes 'always have a limit'; continuous updating needed. prEN 197-6 (cement with recycled materials) under approval � new CEN standard. Gap: no comprehensive high-quality recycled aggregate certification pathway that integrates with REINCARNATE CP-IM provenance data.
